pages.text: Figs ripened on the yard tree. Soft, ripe ones were heavy and hung low.
Lulu took a basket. "I will pick our afternoon snack."
Aunt Rosa hurried over. "The best ones are always high up!"
She poked high branches here and there with a long stick.
Those figs were hard and would not budge. Only the branches swayed.
Aunt Rosa stood on tiptoe, then fell backward with a thump. The figs still hung there.
The basket was empty. Lulu held it and looked up at Aunt Rosa.
Lulu stood by a low, drooping branch and gently twisted off a soft fig.
Plop, plop! Soft figs filled the basket.
Everyone sat in the yard eating figs. Aunt Rosa brought one from high up. It was hard. "Not ready yet," she said.
